hints.title: Track Passenger Queues Chronologically
hints.text: Buses arrive in order of arrival time, and passengers board in chronological order up to bus capacity.

hints.title: Compute Cumulative Waiting Counts
hints.text: Rank the buses by arrival time and compute the count of arriving passengers who arrived before or at each bus arrival time.

hints.title: Use Recursive State Tracking
hints.text: Simulate boarding using a recursive common table expression where each bus boards up to its capacity from remaining waiting passengers.

hints.title: Complete SQL Query
hints.text:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE BusRank AS (
    SELECT 
        bus_id,
        arrival_time,
        capacity,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY arrival_time) AS rn
    FROM Buses
),
BusPassengers AS (
    SELECT 
        b.rn,
        b.bus_id,
        b.capacity,
        COUNT(p.passenger_id) AS total_arrived
    FROM BusRank b
    LEFT JOIN Passengers p ON p.arrival_time <= b.arrival_time
    GROUP BY b.rn, b.bus_id, b.capacity
),
BusNew AS (
    SELECT 
        rn,
        bus_id,
        capacity,
        total_arrived - COALESCE(LAG(total_arrived) OVER (ORDER BY rn), 0) AS new_passengers
    FROM BusPassengers
),
Sim AS (
    SELECT 
        rn,
        bus_id,
        CASE WHEN new_passengers < capacity THEN new_passengers ELSE capacity END AS boarded,
        CASE WHEN new_passengers > capacity THEN new_passengers - capacity ELSE 0 END AS waiting
    FROM BusNew
    WHERE rn = 1
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        b.rn,
        b.bus_id,
        CASE WHEN (s.waiting + b.new_passengers) < b.capacity THEN (s.waiting + b.new_passengers) ELSE b.capacity END AS boarded,
        CASE WHEN (s.waiting + b.new_passengers) > b.capacity THEN (s.waiting + b.new_passengers) - b.capacity ELSE 0 END AS waiting
    FROM Sim s
    JOIN BusNew b ON b.rn = s.rn + 1
)
SELECT bus_id, boarded AS passengers_cnt
FROM Sim
ORDER BY bus_id ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) query execution and joins
variables: N: input size or row count
complexity.whyNaiveFails: A single non-recursive join cannot track stateful passenger spillovers where unboarded passengers roll over to consecutive future buses.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Recursive evaluation takes O(B + P) time and requires O(B) memory for recursion depth matching bus count.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Demonstrate recursive CTE proficiency or procedural simulation to track rolling stateful inventory/capacity.

import pandas as pd

def count_passengers_in_bus(buses: pd.DataFrame, passengers: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if buses.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame({'bus_id': [], 'passengers_cnt': []})
    b_sorted = buses.sort_values('arrival_time').reset_index(drop=True)
    p_sorted = passengers.sort_values('arrival_time')['arrival_time'].tolist()
    boarded_counts = []
    p_idx = 0
    n_p = len(p_sorted)
    for _, bus in b_sorted.iterrows():
        cap = bus['capacity']
        arr = bus['arrival_time']
        eligible = 0
        temp_idx = p_idx
        while temp_idx < n_p and p_sorted[temp_idx] <= arr:
            eligible += 1
            temp_idx += 1
        boarded = min(cap, eligible)
        boarded_counts.append(boarded)
        p_idx += boarded
    b_sorted['passengers_cnt'] = boarded_counts
    return b_sorted[['bus_id', 'passengers_cnt']].sort_values('bus_id')
